added.name: Monzo Bank
added.long_description:
YC has written a good overview of our business on their blog: https://blog.ycombinator.com/monzo-makes-money-work-for-everyone/

Our mission is to make money work for everyone. We are the UK's leading digital bank for individuals and businesses, reinventing the traditional banking industry one customer at a time. We're relentlessly mission driven and always put our customers first - from what products we chose to launch next to our transparency and use of simple language. With a Net Promoter Score of 70+, it shows. 

From our founding in 2015, we now have over 7 million customers in the UK (13% of UK adults) and are building out our team in the US. We've seen incredible organic growth, acquiring 150,000 customers / month in 2022, with 80% of this coming from word of mouth. Our weekly active user rate is ~60% and ~40% of our active users use us as their Main Bank account, showing that we are a product that is embedded in our users' daily lives. We've grown to ~2,450 staff (~400 of which make up the product/tech team), and are backed by YC, Stripe, Tencent, Mike Moritz, and others.

Internally, we encourage an open, collaborative, and inclusive working environment - we were voted the #1 startup where people in the UK want to work for the second year running in 2022. We contribute to open source software, and we continually engage with our wonderful community. We're hiring talented, creative problem-solvers to help us build the bank of the future. Join us!
added.one_liner: A bank as smart as your phone.

Interested in working on an $800B problem? 
Check out our jobs page here: http://jobs.convoy.com/

added.name: Liquid Energy
added.long_description:
Liquid Energy delivers the most scalable and cost effective inference. Our compute is hosted in our proprietary data center modules that we call NanoDC - the Nano Data Center. 

NanoDC is engineered to be rapidly deployable and scalable without traditional bottlenecks like power, permitting, and supply chains. Using NanoDC, Liquid Energy is able to provide the most efficient and sustainable way to scale compute to meet global AI demand.
added.one_liner: Self contained solar-powered AI inference modules: the NanoDC

added.name: Topos
added.long_description: Topos is a neolab founded by two Harvard math dropouts, building agent swarms to bring the rigor and verifiability of mathematics to other fields. Starting in biology, we’re optimizing how agents communicate, formalize problems, and verify each other’s reasoning.

added.name: Nitroduck
added.long_description: We make gene editing easy for all crops. To make pesticides obsolete across vegetables and fruits, enabling coffee to withstand heat waves, making almonds independent of pollinators, pistachios independent of winter chill, and much more. To let breeders create novel, consumer-facing crop varieties like pink pineapples, seedless cherries, and non-browning avocados.
added.one_liner: Monsanto for yummy crops, but without pesticides

added.name: Epsilab
added.long_description: Applied AI research lab focused on RL for frontier model training. Our research and evals cover real-world environment simulation, long-horizon workflows, and multi-player agents, etc.

long_description.before:
Mission: Building insurance products & services focused on lowering the protection gap for the innovation economy on a national and global scale. 

Today, we operate an insurance brokerage focused on startups in AI, robotics, space, and defense. Through the brokerage, we see firsthand where traditional insurance products fail, from AI liability and autonomous systems to defense technology and new space risks.

We are now building proprietary risk models that can price risks even when little historical claims data exists. Our approach uses stochastic simulation, then applies traditional, explainable models to make the output transparent to underwriters and regulators.

This allows us to create new insurance and reinsurance products for emerging industries much faster than traditional carriers.

The U.S. insurance market still relies heavily on foreign reinsurance capacity.
Our goal is to build new reinsurance capacity on American soil for the industries defining the next generation of the U.S. economy, while reducing America's dependence on foreign reinsurance capacity.

long_description.before:
Memoir is building a persistent and proactive AI teammate that helps an entire company keep up with its own progress. Think Instinct but for enterprise. We’re starting with product changes. When engineering ships something, Memoir understands who it affects and creates what each audience needs: a walkthrough for a customer, launch materials for a product marketer, or a technical explanation for another engineering team. It chooses the format and timing, then delivers the approved material in Slack. Nobody has to ask it to start.

We’re beginning with hands-on deployments, learning how each company works and where people depend on one another. That understanding will let Memoir expand beyond product releases to customer commitments, business decisions, and changes across departments. The idea grew from conversations with product marketers struggling to keep up with engineering, and the possibility of extending a proactive personal AI teammate to an entire business. 

Our ambition is a company where every important change sets the right communication in motion: the people affected receive something made for them, when they need it, without someone having to coordinate every handoff. As AI makes individual teams faster, Memoir helps that speed carry through the whole company.
long_description.after:
Memoir is a video call with a proactive AI teammate built in. While people talk, it picks up the work hiding in the conversation and starts on it, in real time. Say "let me pull up the pricing deck" and it appears on your screen. Say "let's sketch the architecture" and a diagram draws itself for everyone. Ask "Memoir, what did we decide on pricing?" and it answers out loud from the call itself, with context gathered beforehand.

When the call ends, the follow-ups are already written: the email to the customer, the calendar hold, the reminder, each one click to send. The work that usually waits hours after a meeting, or never happens, is ready before you hang up.

Agents already work in our inboxes, browsers and code editors. Calls are where teams make decisions, and agents still aren't in the room. We're starting with technical founders on the sales and design calls they host, where a slow follow-up costs a deal, and building toward calls where people and agents work side by side.

one_liner.before: Everything your team ships, explained to everyone it affects.
one_liner.after: The Zoom alternative where agents build what you discuss in real time

long_description.before:
Rex is an AI-native service for order to cash. Rex replaces manual operations with AI agents that continuously manage invoices, customers and exceptions.

Order to cash is a $60B outsourced function because the work is too messy for traditional automation. Every customer has different context, exceptions do not follow clean rules, and the next step is often buried in emails, portals, handoffs, or someone’s memory. Rex agents run continuously in the background and resolve work to SLA standards so cash keeps moving. We're live with pre-IPO tech companies, managing  >$500m in receivables from F100 companies, cutting manual follow-up cycles from weeks to hours.

We founded Rex after spending four years building Sequence, an a16z-backed finance ops platform, from zero to Series A — where we saw firsthand that at-scale, O2C still runs on manual labour.

Rex is the #1 winner of the Vercel AI Accelerator out of 2,500 teams, selected by Guillermo Rauch and leaders from OpenAI, Anthropic, Browserbase and more.
